newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sons of Gwalia lifts Q2 gold output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sons of Gwalia lifts Q2 gold output.

text.p: Sons of Gwalia Ltd said on Wednesday it produced a group record 132,987 ounces of gold in the December quarter, up 17 percent from the September quarter.

The Western Australia-based miner also said that a substantial increase in its gold hedging book in the second quarter takes its forward sales position to a current 3.2 million ounces. "This will result in the company's estimated gold production over the next six months, at current levels, being sold at approximately A$640 an ounce," Sons of Gwalia said in its second quarter activities report.
This compares with 1.7 million ounces hedged forward as of September 30, 1996 at an average price of A$645.00 an ounce.
At the company's Sons of Gwalia mine near Leonora, where underground trial mining was started in December, gold production reached a company record 40,233 ounces.
Gold production estimates at the mine for the year ending June 30, 1997 is unchanged at 138,000 ounces, the company said.
At the Marvel Loch mine, where output of 26,493 ounces in the second quarter exceeded budget, operations are on track to produce 120,000 ounces in 1996/97, Sons of Gwalia said.
At Marvel Loch, first stage cut-back work was providing better grades and ore continuity at depth, Sons of Gwalia said.
Drilling at depth provided further encouraging results including 10 metres at 3.03 gammes of gold a tonne, 13 metres at 3.38 g/t and 22 metres at 2.06 g/t.
Gold production from the Bullfinch mine was a disappointing 20,972 ounces, the company said.
Production from the Copperhead mine at Bullfinch was hampered by insufficient high grade ore being available from the current cut-back which is behind schedule.

This was combined with lower-than-budgeted head grade from the Golden Pig and Fraser's mines as a large percentage of the ore produced and milled at Bullfinch came from development ore, Sons of Gwalia said.
Gold production estimates for the 1996/1997 financial year are between 110,000 and 120,000 ounces, it said.
Gold production at the company's 76.9 percent owned Yilgarn Star substantially exceeded budget and was a record 37,529 ounces, the company said.
At the laverton project, gold production for the quarter was 8,291 ounces.

The Laverton ore treated during the quarter was from low grade satellite pits pending development of a new large pit close to the mill, resulting in marginally lower than budgeted production, Sons of Gwalia said.
The 49 percent owned Salsigne mine in France produced 16,629 fine ounces for the quarter, the company said.
Overall cash production costs for Sons of Gwalia averaged A$352 an ounce in the second quarter, the company said. Son of Gwalia did not previously issue its costs of production.
